blocks.text: A.10 Chapter 3 Periodic Classification of Elements

1. Element X belongs to VII-A group and third
period. Third period elements are called typi-
cal elements.
Hence, the correct option is (a).

2. Oxidizing property is directly proportional to
electro negativity and electron affinity. There-
fore, fluorine is a good oxidizing agent.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

3. According to the law of triads, the average of
atomic weights of Be and Ca is equal to the
atomic weight of Mg.

Hence, the correct option is (b).

4. A → He, B → Cs, C → Cl, D → F
Maximum metallic character is Cs.
Maximum electronegativity is F.
Maximum electron affinity is Cl.
Maximum ionization energy is He.
Hence, the correct option is (a).

5. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \text{I-A}$ group and cation formed is $\mathrm{A}^{+1}$ ($\mathrm{Na}^{+1}$).
$\mathrm{B} \rightarrow \text{II-A}$ group and cation formed is $\mathrm{B}^{+2}$ ($\mathrm{Mg}^{+2}$).
$\mathrm{C} \rightarrow \text{VII-A}$ group and anion formed is $\mathrm{C}^{-1}$ ($\overline{\mathrm{Cl}}$).
$\mathrm{D} \rightarrow \text{VI-A}$ group and anion formed is $\mathrm{D}^{-2}$ ($\mathrm{S}^{-2}$).
$\therefore$ Increasing order of sizes is CDBA.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

6. Caesium belongs to very long period.
Xeon belongs to second long period.
Potassium belongs to long period.
Radium belongs to incomplete period.
Hence, the correct option is (b).

7. Across the period, ionization energy increases
due to decrease in atomic size. Due to stable
valence electronic configuration of II-A group
elements, they possess higher I.P values than
corresponding III-A group elements.
Hence, the correct option is (b).

8. Across the period, electron affinity increases
due to decrease in atomic size. The 18th group
elements possess zero electron affinity values
due to stable octet configuration.
Hence, the correct option is (a).

9. Drastic increase in the second and fourth I.P
values indicates the two elements A and B
belong to I-A and III-A groups, respectively.
Hence, the correct option is (a).

10. Electronic configuration of element belongs to
the third period and IV-A group is 2, 8, and 4.
$\therefore$ Difference in electrons = $8 - 4 = 4$
Hence, the correct option is (c).

11. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow 2, 8, 8, 1 \Rightarrow$ 4th period and I-A group
$\mathrm{B} \rightarrow 2, 8, 6 \Rightarrow$ 3rd period VI-A group
$\mathrm{C} \rightarrow 2, 8, 1 \Rightarrow$ 3rd period I-A group
$\mathrm{D} \rightarrow 2, 5 \Rightarrow$ 2nd period and V-A group
$\mathrm{E} \rightarrow 2, 8, 18, 8, 2 \Rightarrow$ 5th period II-A group
The correct order of atomic sizes is $\mathrm{E} > \mathrm{A} > \mathrm{C}$
$> \mathrm{B} > \mathrm{D}$.
Hence, the correct option is (b).

12. Element A is Ba and B is Rb. I.P of Ba is less
than that of Rb.

Hence, the correct option is (d).

13. In case of iso electronic species, with increase
in charge of anion, effective nuclear charge
decreases and hence, ionic size increases. In
case of cations it is exactly reverse.
Hence, the correct option is (d).

14. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}$ and belongs to III-A group and 3rd
period.
$\mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ge}$ and belongs to IV-A group and 4th
period.
$\mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{Si}$ and belongs to IV-A group and 3rd
period.
